MN202610_18h1ynvl0ih.t:
KIGALI – Rwanda’s U-17 national team held off a determined Ethiopia 2-1 to secure qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) in Morocco, recovering from the disappointment of their semi-final elimination to achieve the tournament’s main objective.

The Amavubi juniors made a flying start at Kigali Pelé Stadium on Monday, scoring twice in the opening 16 minutes before Ethiopia pulled one back shortly before half-time.

Rwanda struck early when Heylen Jayden Shema fired home in the fifth minute, finishing off an assist from Pacifique Bahati. Shema, who had largely been used as a substitute in previous matches, was handed a starting role and made an immediate impact.

The junior wasps continued to press, forcing Ethiopia into a defensive scramble before winning a corner in the 15th minute. The pressure paid off when Isaac Ndizeye scored from the resulting set piece to double Rwanda’s lead.

The hosts then had to withstand sustained pressure in the second half to protect their advantage and book their place at the continental tournament.

Head coach Jimmy Murisa said the qualification is evidence of progress in youth football after years of investment and development.

“It’s been a process of development, lots of investments, so I would say these are the kinds of fruits you could just be happy of. To see ourselves, first assignment, qualifying for the African Cup of Nations, it’s a big achievement,” Murisa said after the match.

Rwanda had entered the third-place play-off after losing to Somalia on penalties in the semi-finals, missing the chance to contest the regional title. Monday’s match therefore offered the young team another opportunity to deliver on its primary target of reaching AFCON.

The hosts wasted little time asserting themselves but Ethiopia also refused to surrender.

The Walyas gradually found a way back into the contest and gave Rwanda a nervy finish to the first half when Akrem Abduselam headed home two minutes before the interval, cutting the deficit to 2-1.

With the advantage reduced to a single goal, Rwanda had to approach the second half differently, balancing its attacking ambitions with the need to protect the lead.

As the contest wore on, Ethiopia made substitutions in an attempt to increase the pressure, but Rwanda remained organized.

Pacifique Bahati came close to extending the lead late in the game, sending an effort narrowly wide, while Ethiopia also failed to convert its remaining opportunities.

Ethiopia kept their push for an equalizer, but the Amavubi maintained their defensive discipline and held on until the final whistle to secure qualification for AFCON U-17 in Morocco.

Despite celebrating the achievement, Murisa acknowledged that his team had fallen short of its ambition to win the regional tournament. Rwanda’s performances had improved as the competition progressed, raising hopes of a place in the final before the defeat to Somalia.

“Our main objective was to qualify, but I think we had an opportunity. If you could see, as we played our first game, the second game, my players started having that confidence. Then we started being title contenders,” he said.

The coach said the tournament had exposed his young players to the demands of competitive international football, including the pressure that can affect decision-making at crucial moments.

For a squad still developing, he believes those experiences will be important as preparations begin for AFCON. The next task, Murisa said, is to ensure Rwanda arrive in Morocco ready to compete rather than simply participate.

“Prepare well. Play more competitive games so that you get to that level,” Murisa said, calling for exposure to high-level opposition ahead of the continental tournament.

He also credited the Rwanda Football Federation and the Ministry of Sports for supporting the team’s progress.

Rwanda’s qualification marks their return to the AFCON U-17 finals for the first time since 2011, when they hosted the tournament and finished runners-up. A year before the team had qualified for the world cup.

The latest achievement gives this generation of young players an opportunity to build on that history, with the challenge now shifting from securing a place at the finals to proving themselves against Africa’s best.

MN202610_xant9nbr0p.t:
Imirimo yo kubaka uruganda rw’amazi ruzwi nka “Kagaga Water Supply System” ruzatanga metero kibe zirenga 12,000 ku munsi yatangiye mu karere ka Muhanga.

Urwo ruganda rw’amazi rugiye kubakwa mu Mudugudu wa Murama, Akagari ka Remera, Umurenge wa Muhanga.

Imirimo yo kurwubaka yabanjirijwe no kwimura bamwe mu baturage bahaturiye, kubaka inzu abakozi bacumbikamo no gutunganya ahazajya urugomero rw’amazi aturuka mu mugezi wa Kagaga agahura n’aturuka mu wa Makurungwe.

Ayo mazi yose amena mu mugezi mugari wa Bakokwe, ni yo azajya muri uru ruganda rw’amazi.

Eng Dr Bagaragaza Romuald ukora muri Kampani y’Abashinwa yatsindiye isoko ryo gukora iyo mirimo, yabwiye UMUSEKE ko uruganda rw’amazi bagiye kubaka ruzatanga metero kibe zirenga 12,000 ku munsi.

Ati: “Imirimo yo kubaka uruganda rutunganya amazi nirangira duteganya kubaka ikigega kinini cy’amazi kizayakwirakwiza mu Mirenge itandukanye y’Umujyi wa Muhanga, ndetse n’indi 4 y’Akarere ka Kamonyi.”

Dr Bagaragaza yongeraho ko usibye ikigega bateganya kubaka, bafite ibikoresho bizifashishwa kongera ingano y’amazi akaba menshi mu miyoboro isanzwe WASAC yashyizeho.

Mujawamariya Médiatrice, umwe mu baturage avuga ko babariwe imitungo yabo bahafite bakaba bategereje kubona ingurane kugira ngo bimuke.

Ati: “Icyifuzo cyacu ni uko WASAC iduha ingurane kugira ngo twimuke vuba.”

Mujawamariya avuga ko uko amafaranga y’ingurane akomeza gutinda bidindiza ibikorwa byabo by’ubuhinzi.

Iyakaremye Libératha avuga ko bishimira iki gikorwa remezo kuko abatari bafite amazi n’abavomaga mu kabande bagiye kuyabona hafi.

Ati: “Twavomaga mu nkengero z’ahagiye kubakwa uruganda, ubu noneho barayatwegereje.”

Meya w’Akarere ka Muhanga, Kayitare Jacqueline avuga ko uruganda rw’amazi ruziye igihe, kuko ubusanzwe Umujyi wa Muhanga umaze gukura, kandi ukaba utajyana n’ubwiyongere bw’abawutuye.

Ati: “Umushinga ww’Akagaga tuwutegerejeho igisubizo cy’amazi akenewe cyane ku baturage bo mu Mujyi no mu bice biwukikije.”

Yakomeje agira ati: “Twifuza ko kubarira abaturage imitungo yabo bikorwa mu bushishozi, kugira ngo hatabaho kwibeshya hakagira abarengana cyangwa bagahabwa ingurane itajyanye n’imitungo bahafite.”

Kayitare akavuga ko bafite umugenagaciro wa Leta uzabara ibikorwa bijyanye n’imitungo y’abaturage, akabishyikiriza Inama Njyanama y’Akarere ikabyemeza.

Gusa nubwo bimeze bityo hari bamwe mu baturage bamaze guhabwa ingurane y’imitungo yabo bari bahafite, bamwe bakaba barangije kubaka inzu zo kubamo, abandi bakavuga ko batangiye imishinga y’ubucukuzi n’ubworozi bakesha amafaranga bahawe.

Imirimo yo kubaka uruganda rw’amazi rwa Kagaga izarangira itwaye arenga miliyari 20Frw, bikaba biteganyijwe ko rushobora kuba rutanga amazi mu mwaka wa 2030.

MN202610_8mob74i87i.t:
Mu gihe Isi ikomeje guhangana n’ibibazo bireba imiryango, umuhanzi w’indirimbo zo kuramya no guhimbaza Imana, Alexis Dusabe ari kwitegura urugendo rw’igitaramo kitwa ‘The hope uk worship & restore’, kizabera i Coventry mu Bwongereza.

Muri iki gitaramo azaba ari umwanya w’ibiganiro bigamije kubaka imiryango, n’umwanya wihariye wo kuramya no guhimbaza Imana. Uyu muramyi, azaba ari kumwe na Pasiteri Dr. Antoine Rutayisire.

Alex Dusabe aganira na UMUSEKE yavuze ko iki gitaramo kizaba kiri mu rwego rwo gukomeza ingo zikubakira ku ijambo ry’Imana, no kugarurira abantu ibyiringiro.

Ati “Ni urugendo rwo ku wa 19 Ukuboza 2026, ni ubutumwa bugamije gukomeza ingo, gufasha abantu kongera kubona ibyiringiro, no gushishikariza imiryango kubakira ku mahame y’ijambo ry’Imana.”

Uyu muhanzi yahamirije UMUSEKE ko ari ubwambere zaba ageze mu gihugu cy’u Bwongereza, bityo asaba abakunzi be kuzitabira ari benshi bakabwira n’abandi ko kwinjira ari ubntu, ko yiteguye kubasusurutsa, bityo arararikira Abanyarwanda, Abarundi n’abandi batuye mu Bwongereza, no mu bindi bihugu by’u Burayi, cyane cyane abitegura kurushinga, abubatse ingo, imiryango inyura mu bihe bikomeye n’abifuza gukomeza ubuzima bwabo bwo mu mwuka, kuzitabira uru rugendo rwihariye.

Ati: “Ni ubwa mbere nzaba ngeze muri iki gihugu cy’u Bwongereza, niteguye gufasha abakunzi banjye gususuruka, bazaze ari benshi babwire n’abandi kwinjira ni ubuntu.”

Ibi bije bikurikira isohoka ry’indirimbo nshya ya Alexis Dusabe, yitwa “Mfite umukunzi”, ikaba ari yo ndirimbo y’uyu muhanzi yatangiriyeho urugendo rwe rwo kuramya no guhimbaza Imana, icyo gihe hari mu mwaka 2000, iboneka kuri YouTube channel ye Alexis Dusabe Official.

Ni indirimbo y’imbaraga iryoshye ishimangira urukundo rwa Yesu Kristo n’instinzi ye by’iteka ryose.

Uyu muririmbyi w’indirimbo zo kuramya no guhibaza Imana, yakoze ibitaramo bitandukanye hirya no hino by’ivugabutumwa rinyuze mu ndirimbo, yigaruriye imitima ya benshi umwaka ushize wa 2025 yizihije imyaka 25 amaze ari umuramyi.

Mu bantu bazwi cyane mu ivugabutumwa bazitabira iki gitaramo barimo Rev. Dr. Pasiteri Antoine Rutayisire, umwe mu bashumba n’abigisha b’ijambo ry’Imana bazwi mu Rwanda no hanze yarwo.

MN202610_8kvobioksc.t:
The relationship between the two main characters, Jason and Lucia, is at the centre of Rockstar's latest Grand Theft Auto title

Imagine your partner spending hours flirting with someone else, trying to hold their hand and taking them on dates. Most people would have questions.

But what if that someone only exists inside a video game?

The latest instalment in Rockstar's blockbuster Grand Theft Auto franchise is set to be the biggest entertainment launch of the year when it is released next month.

Judging by previews, the connection between its two main characters is a central feature.

Rockstar has hinted that the Bonnie and Clyde-type protagonists Jason and Lucia do not have to become a full-on romantic couple.

But their relationship can grow by spending time together outside of the main crime and life-on-the-run storyline – through shopping, visiting bars and restaurants and working out together.

Smaller interactions like holding hands and quickly responding to each other's texts can help build a bond.

The idea has restarted a debate almost as old as gaming itself: if you are that invested in a fictional relationship, is your real-life partner entitled to be upset?

In September, polling company YouGov put that question to more than 4,000 British adults.

About 6% said they would regard it as cheating, while a further 19% said they would "not be okay with it". Women were considerably more likely than men to take a dim view.

Alli Franco, a 30-year-old Texan who posts anime and gaming content to more than a million followers , external on TikTok, says she felt "dismayed" watching the debate unfold online.

"If your partner is insecure about a fictional character, then there needs to be some serious reflection," she told the BBC.

"It's similar to having a crush on a TV star, but even further removed from cheating since there is no other actual person involved.”

After Franco posted a video on the subject, hundreds of commenters appeared to agree with her, although some did have reservations.

"To be honest, it depends," wrote one. "If you're cancelling plans with your significant other or directing your intimacy towards a fictional character, then that is a little odd."

"It's very odd and it really gives me the ick," one woman told us.

Can you cheat on your partner in a video game character?

GTA 6 - all you need to know about Rockstar's blockbuster game

GTA 6 will cost £70 - and physical edition will not contain a disc

For decades, video games have allowed players to build relationships with non-player characters, or NPCs.

Gamers could marry villagers in Harvest Moon in 1996, shape emotional storylines in Final Fantasy VII and pursue more complex romances in role-playing games like Baldur's Gate II.

In life simulator The Sims, they could flirt, date, marry and have children with computer-controlled characters.

But all those interactions were tightly scripted, based on rules and storylines written in advance by game developers.

GTA 6 appears to offer something more dynamic, allowing players to shape the relationship between Jason and Lucia through a wider range of open-world interactions and choices.

"The more sophisticated games get, the less likely it is that players get pulled out of the experience," says Arienne Ferchaud, an associate professor at Florida State University who studies how people form connections with fictional characters.

"Games are doing a better job of mimicking reality and mimicking social relationships."

Rockstar has said players do not have to build a romantic connection in the game

Grand Theft Auto 6 may represent the current cutting edge of game design, but the next leap forward could come from artificial intelligence.

Nvidia, Ubisoft and other huge tech companies are already experimenting with generative AI systems that allow players to hold more natural conversations with NPCs.

Future characters could remember past encounters, react to a player's actions and build relationships that change over time rather than following a pre-written script.

Ferchaud believes that could make games feel even more immersive.

"You could have relationships that feel more solid or more special," she says, although she argues AI as it exists today would still be creating "a stronger illusion" rather than a genuinely meaningful connection.

Whether that is exciting or unsettling may depend on the player, and there has been some resistance to the wider use of the technology in gaming .

Franco says she is already seeing adverts for AI chatbots that let fans talk to their favourite anime characters.

"I can definitely see AI integrating into games and making it a more realistic experience," she says.

"But should that happen I would still see it as just a game. At the end of the day you can't cheat with lines of code."

TorchNeuron provides a new native backend for PyTorch on AWS Trainium. Transformers, Diffusers and Kernels natively support it, making it easier than ever to run models on Trainium and to share them on the HF hub.

TorchNeuron is a PyTorch plugin that brings a new backend for Trainium enabling support for eager mode, torch.compile and native distributed APIs like FSDP and TP. Read the Pytorch blog to learn more about TorchNeuron.

Starting Oct. 20, 2026, TorchNeuron will be available as a public beta. Researchers and developers will be able to install it with pip install torch-neuronx .

To date, the Hugging Face experience on AWS Trainium and Inferentia — AI chips designed respectively for cost-effective training and inference at scale — has been delivered through optimum-neuron . This library relies on the torch-neuronx package, which is based on PyTorch XLA. It was the natural choice at the time, but it meant thinking like a compiler: lazy tensors instead of eager execution, static shapes only, a recompilation for every graph break. Optimum Neuron existed to hide that complexity, and maintained custom code (modeling classes, trainers, etc) to do so.

TorchNeuron changes this. It integrates directly into PyTorch and exposes neuron as a native device, with eager execution, PyTorch's own distributed primitives (DTensor, FSDP2) and torch.compile .

For the Hugging Face libraries, Trainium becomes a device like any other: Transformers, Diffusers, Accelerate, PEFT and TRL run on it directly, with the same classes and scripts you would use on any other accelerator. From now on, we recommend that Neuron users use these libraries directly instead of going through Optimum Neuron.

Text generation is now natively supported in Transformers for a wide range of models. With TorchNeuron, 89% of the top 100 most-used text-generation model architectures are supported out of the box, compared to 46% with Optimum Neuron v0.4.5. You just need to pass the device_map=neuron argument in your code and your model will be moved to the Neuron devices.

The following is an example of text-generation with tensor parallelism, which will enable to fully benefit from your Neuron instance. Note that it uses a static cache for generation as this is strongly recommended with Neuron to prevent frequent recompilations.

Now that Neuron is a native PyTorch device, training on Trainium uses the same Hugging Face libraries as any other accelerator: Transformers, Accelerate, PEFT and TRL. You no longer need a dedicated trainer or a Neuron-specific fork of the model code. A standard TRL fine-tuning script runs on a Trainium instance with only a few Neuron-specific settings.

Here is a supervised fine-tuning script built on TRL's SFTTrainer . If you have fine-tuned a model with TRL on GPUs before, it should look familiar.

Parallelism is handled natively by Transformers. You put a DistributedConfig with the tensor-parallel (TP) and FSDP sizes in model_init_kwargs , SFTTrainer passes it to from_pretrained , and the model is sharded as its weights are loaded. The Trainer sees that the model is already distributed and does not wrap it again. You don't need an --fsdp flag or an Accelerate FSDP config.

Nothing in the script is tied to Trainium: the same code runs on any hardware. A few things are worth knowing when you run it on Trainium:

The command below launches training with torchrun , which starts one process per NeuronCore. TP_SIZE and FSDP_SIZE set the parallelism layout, and their product is the number of processes: here 4 x 8 = 32, matching --nproc_per_node . The 32 processes form a 4 x 8 grid. Tensor parallelism splits each layer across the 4 cores of a TP group, and FSDP shards the parameters, gradients and optimizer state across the 8 TP groups.

We ran it on 8 Trainium2 chips (32 NeuronCores), which is half a trn2.48xlarge instance.

Training runs to completion, and trainer.save_model writes a standard Transformers checkpoint. Nothing in it is tied to Neuron: you can push it to the Hugging Face Hub as is and load it on any other hardware.

Many pipelines from the Diffusers library are compatible with TorchNeuron in eager and compiled mode. FLUX.1-dev, FLUX.2, Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-2.1 and H3 are also compatible with tensor parallelism to make the most of your Neuron devices. The following is an example showing how you can use TP:

You can run this piece of code with: NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2 torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 run.py .

More and more pipleines will be compatible with TP. If a pipeline you like is not, you can also add support for it following this guide .

Make sure to check out the kernels from the Neuron team as more and more Neuron kernels will become available on the Hub to speed up your models. Neuron kernels can be written using the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI), which gives lower control to optimize operations. This way, users can run their own custom operations and share them on the hub.

You can use for example this kernel to speed up your vision transformers with up to a x2.4 speedup on Trainium!

Special thanks to the AWS team for their work on TorchNeuron and for their reactivity to our feedback to make the HF integration as good as possible.

MN202610_1dfyaynr7fh.t:
El Mansouri (left) was named by King Mohammed VI (right) as the country's first female prime minister

The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister.

Mustafa Ramid, a former justice minister in an Islamist-led government, cited the saying earlier this month, in a lengthy Facebook post questioning whether a woman should hold the country's highest political office.

He argued that Morocco, a Muslim majority country, had found a balance between equality and the responsibilities of state leadership, as the highest office - that of the king - continued to be reserved for men.

Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy. Yet executive power remains in the hands of the 63-year-old monarch.

El Mansouri's Authenticity and Modernity Party (Pam) won the most seats in September's parliamentary election and has since announced a coalition with three other parties. Together, they hold 207 of the 395 seats in parliament.

El Mansouri, 50, presented her appointment as a milestone for Moroccan women

El Mansouri's royal appointment was historic but it exposed persistent reservations about women in positions of power.

The day after her appointment, local broadcaster Chouf TV took to the streets to ask Moroccan men "what they thought" of a woman heading the government.

Several men, mostly middle-aged or older, hesitated before answering. Some said they accepted the decision because it was the king's choice.

One grey-haired man, who did not give his name or age, said: "It feels strange to have a woman as head of government. I'm not sure if it sits well with me."

Criticism of the monarchy carries legal risks in Morocco. The penal code criminalises certain forms of offence or insult against the king, the royal family and the monarchy.

Online, the appointment became fodder for political satire.

A video showing two women pulling each other's hair was widely shared, with captions suggesting that this is what parliamentary disagreements between El Mansouri and her colleagues might look like.

However many younger Moroccans, especially women, welcomed her appointment.

While attitudes are changing in Morocco, conservative, religious views still hold great weight.

Some of the country's most contentious debates over gender equality centre on family law, including inheritance, marriage and divorce.

Under existing inheritance rules, a daughter typically receives half the share of a son in comparable circumstances.

The Higher Council of Ulemas, the country's body of religious scholars, has resisted calls for equal inheritance, citing Islamic jurisprudence.

It has also rejected proposals to abolish taasib, a rule that can require female orphans without brothers to share their inheritance with male relatives, including distant ones.

In a 2022 report, Morocco's National Human Rights Council said unequal inheritance rules contributed to poverty among women.

Polygamy is also legal under certain conditions. Proposed changes to the family code have included allowing women to stipulate in their marriage contracts that their husbands cannot take another wife.

But exceptions remain, including provisions relating to a first wife's infertility or illness, which women's rights groups have criticised on grounds of privacy and medical confidentiality.

These issues are at the heart of proposals to reform the Moudawana, Morocco's family code, which governs marriage, divorce and child custody.

A package of changes was announced in 2024, but the reforms have yet to become law.

As well as family law, some young women hope the new prime minister will try to improve education for girls.

Morocco's High Commission for Planning, the country's official national statistics agency, found in 2025 that just 55% of girls aged 15–17 were going to school in rural areas, where poverty, early marriage and dropping out of school remain key barriers. In urban areas, it was 100%.

"Many girls in rural Morocco drop out of school early because schools are far away, transport is unsafe or unavailable, and families with limited means often keep their daughters at home," Chifae Laazouzi, a young Moroccan woman, tells the BBC.

She says one reason is that many girls in poor and rural areas cannot afford menstrual sanitary products.

"Menstrual health is still treated as a taboo... I would like to see free menstrual products in schools," Laazouzi says.

El Mansouri is no newcomer to politics. Over more than two decades in public life, she has served as mayor of Marrakech, held government posts and sat in parliament.

For the past five years, she served as minister for national territory planning, urban planning, housing and city policy under the previous Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch.

After her appointment, El Mansouri presented the moment as a milestone for Moroccan women.

"Being the first female head of government is not just a source of pride for me, but for all the women of the kingdom," she said.

Since her appointment, she has not indicated whether she plans to try and push through the reforms to the family code.

In her political career so far, she has not made any prominent public statements about women's rights, even while changes to inheritance rules, polygamy and the family code were being widely debated.

The king of Morocco, Mohammed VI, holds the title of Commander of the Faithful, a traditional Islamic title embedded in the Moroccan constitution

Dr Irene Fernandez-Molina, an expert on the Global South at the University of Exeter in the UK, sees the appointment in the context of the monarchy's broader political interests.

"Two headlines have dominated coverage of [September's] parliamentary election in Morocco: a two-decade low turnout and King Mohammed VI's appointment of a woman as prime minister for the first time in this country's history," she tells the BBC.

"The latter cannot be understood without the former."

Official figures put turnout at just 38% of registered voters, while the proportion of all eligible voters who cast a ballot was even lower.

Fernandez-Molina describes the appointment as an example of "authoritarian state feminism, a top-down, selective instrumentalisation of the struggle for women's rights for regime legitimation purposes".

She argues that promoting a woman to the highest government office might be intended to project an image of modernisation and progress, even when the political system and the pace of social reform remain largely unchanged.

For Moroccan women's rights advocate Yasmina Benslimane, the appointment breaks a longstanding barrier, but says El Mansouri's background is also important.

"It does challenge stereotypes, because it finally breaks a ceiling that was never broken," she says. "But it matters how she got there."

El Mansouri's late father was a pasha, a senior local official, and a diplomat. Benslimane argues that her privileged background and access to political networks distinguish her from many Moroccan women who have fewer opportunities to enter public life.

For Benslimane, like many women's rights groups in the country, reform of the Moudawana remains a key test of the new government.

However, El Mansouri's room for manoeuvre is shaped by the country's political system.

The king retains extensive powers over key areas, including defence and foreign affairs, while the head of government operates within a system where authority is shared.

When it comes to Moudawana reform, she would have to face the country's religious scholars, who are mostly men.

While some Moroccan women welcome her appointment, they say it is what she does as prime minister that really counts.

"I don't think El Mansouri should be judged by the fact that she is a woman. Being a woman in power doesn't automatically make someone a champion of women's rights," Sara Zouiten, a young Moroccan woman, tells the BBC.

"Her party presents itself as a modernising political force, so I want to see whether that translates into actual change."
